# Linkerd2 Overview

Relevant source files

  * [ADOPTERS.md](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/ADOPTERS.md)
  * [CHANGES.md](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/CHANGES.md)

  * [viz/charts/linkerd-viz/Chart.yaml](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/viz/charts/linkerd-viz/Chart.yaml)



## Purpose and Scope

This document provides a high-level overview of Linkerd2, a service mesh platform that provides observability, reliability, and security for microservices without requiring application code changes. This overview covers the system's architecture, core components, and key capabilities.

For detailed information about specific subsystems, see [Architecture](/linkerd/linkerd2/2-architecture), [Components](/linkerd/linkerd2/3-components), [Deployment](/linkerd/linkerd2/4-deployment), and [Extensions](/linkerd/linkerd2/5-extensions).

## What is Linkerd2

Linkerd2 is a service mesh designed to give platform-wide observability, reliability, and security without requiring configuration or code changes. It operates by injecting lightweight proxy sidecars into Kubernetes pods that intercept and manage all network traffic between services.

The system consists of two main planes:

  * **Control Plane** : Manages configuration, service discovery, and policy enforcement
  * **Data Plane** : Handles actual traffic routing and observability through injected proxies



Linkerd2 supports over 100 organizations in production environments, ranging from small startups to large enterprises like Microsoft, Docker, and Nordstrom.

_Sources:[ ADOPTERS.md1-106](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/ADOPTERS.md#L1-L106) [charts/linkerd-control-plane/Chart.yaml4-6](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/charts/linkerd-control-plane/Chart.yaml#L4-L6)_

## System Architecture

The following diagram illustrates Linkerd2's high-level architecture and component relationships:

### Linkerd2 System Architecture


_Sources:[ charts/linkerd-control-plane/Chart.yaml1-25](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/charts/linkerd-control-plane/Chart.yaml#L1-L25) [viz/charts/linkerd-viz/Chart.yaml1-20](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/viz/charts/linkerd-viz/Chart.yaml#L1-L20) [multicluster/charts/linkerd-multicluster/Chart.yaml1-20](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/multicluster/charts/linkerd-multicluster/Chart.yaml#L1-L20) [jaeger/charts/linkerd-jaeger/Chart.yaml1-20](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/jaeger/charts/linkerd-jaeger/Chart.yaml#L1-L20)_

## Core Components

### Control Plane Components

Component| Purpose| Key Functions  
---|---|---  
`linkerd-identity`| Certificate Authority| Issues and manages mTLS certificates for workload identity  
`linkerd-destination`| Service Discovery| Provides endpoint discovery and traffic routing information  
`linkerd-policy-controller`| Traffic Policy| Enforces authorization policies and traffic rules  
`linkerd-proxy-injector`| Sidecar Injection| Automatically injects proxy sidecars via Kubernetes admission webhooks  
  
### Data Plane Components

Component| Purpose| Technology  
---|---|---  
`linkerd2-proxy`| Sidecar Proxy| Rust-based proxy handling all service-to-service communication  
`linkerd-init`| Network Setup| Configures iptables rules to redirect traffic through the proxy  
  
_Sources:[ charts/linkerd-control-plane/Chart.yaml4-6](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/charts/linkerd-control-plane/Chart.yaml#L4-L6) [charts/linkerd2-cni/Chart.yaml4-8](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/charts/linkerd2-cni/Chart.yaml#L4-L8)_

## Key Capabilities

### Service Mesh Features

**Observability** : Linkerd2 provides automatic metrics collection, distributed tracing, and traffic visualization without requiring application changes. The `linkerd-viz` extension adds Prometheus metrics collection and a web-based dashboard.

**Security** : Automatic mutual TLS (mTLS) encryption between services with certificate rotation handled by the `linkerd-identity` controller. Policy-based authorization controls which services can communicate.

**Reliability** : Traffic management features including load balancing, circuit breaking, retries, and timeouts configured through the `linkerd-policy-controller`.

**Multi-cluster** : The `linkerd-multicluster` extension enables secure service-to-service communication across Kubernetes clusters with service discovery and traffic routing.

### Code Structure Overview


The codebase is primarily written in Go for control plane components, Rust for the policy controller, and JavaScript/React for the web dashboard. Deployment is managed through Helm charts and generated Kubernetes manifests.

_Sources:[ CHANGES.md1-10](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/CHANGES.md#L1-L10) [charts/linkerd-control-plane/Chart.yaml12-25](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/charts/linkerd-control-plane/Chart.yaml#L12-L25) [viz/charts/linkerd-viz/Chart.yaml11-20](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/viz/charts/linkerd-viz/Chart.yaml#L11-L20)_

## Release and Versioning

Linkerd2 follows a regular release cycle with both stable and edge releases. The project has transitioned to using GitHub's automated release notes feature for tracking changes and improvements.

Recent stable releases include features like:

  * Native sidecar container support for Kubernetes 1.29+
  * Gateway API HTTPRoute support
  * Direct pod-to-pod multicluster communication
  * Enhanced policy enforcement and traffic management



_Sources:[ CHANGES.md4-12](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/CHANGES.md#L4-L12) [CHANGES.md513-534](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/CHANGES.md#L513-L534)_

## Extensions Ecosystem

Linkerd2 supports a modular extension system that adds optional functionality:

  * **Viz Extension** : Observability dashboard with Prometheus, Grafana, and metrics visualization
  * **Multicluster Extension** : Cross-cluster service mesh capabilities with gateway-based or direct pod-to-pod communication
  * **Jaeger Extension** : Distributed tracing integration using OpenCensus and Jaeger



Each extension is packaged as a separate Helm chart and can be installed independently based on operational requirements.

_Sources:[ viz/charts/linkerd-viz/Chart.yaml4-6](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/viz/charts/linkerd-viz/Chart.yaml#L4-L6) [multicluster/charts/linkerd-multicluster/Chart.yaml4-6](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/multicluster/charts/linkerd-multicluster/Chart.yaml#L4-L6) [jaeger/charts/linkerd-jaeger/Chart.yaml4-6](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/jaeger/charts/linkerd-jaeger/Chart.yaml#L4-L6)_

This document describes the overall system architecture of Linkerd2, including its control plane, data plane, and key subsystems. It covers the core components that enable service mesh functionality and their interactions within a Kubernetes cluster.

For information about specific components like the CLI tool, see [CLI Tool](/linkerd/linkerd2/3.1-cli-tool). For deployment patterns and installation details, see [Deployment](/linkerd/linkerd2/4-deployment).

## System Overview

Linkerd2 implements a service mesh architecture that consists of a control plane managing mesh-wide concerns and a data plane of lightweight proxies handling traffic. The system is designed as a collection of Kubernetes controllers and custom resources that work together to provide transparent service-to-service communication, security, and observability.


Sources: [cli/cmd/testdata/install_default.golden1-2000](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/testdata/install_default.golden#L1-L2000) [controller/api/destination/server.go44-61](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/server.go#L44-L61) [controller/cmd/destination/main.go1-50](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/cmd/destination/main.go#L1-L50)

## Control Plane Architecture

The control plane consists of several specialized controllers that manage different aspects of the service mesh. Each controller runs as a separate Kubernetes Deployment with its own service account and RBAC permissions.


Sources: [cli/cmd/testdata/install_default.golden17-120](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/testdata/install_default.golden#L17-L120) [controller/api/destination/watcher/endpoints_watcher.go84-106](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/watcher/endpoints_watcher.go#L84-L106) [controller/api/destination/server.go44-61](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/server.go#L44-L61)

### Identity Controller

The `linkerd-identity` controller serves as the cluster's Certificate Authority, issuing short-lived mTLS certificates to workloads in the mesh. It implements the `identity` gRPC service defined in the proxy API.

Component| Function| Port  
---|---|---  
`identity` container| Issues and validates mTLS certificates| 8080 (gRPC)  
`linkerd-identity-issuer` Secret| Stores CA private key and certificate| -  
`linkerd-identity-trust-roots` ConfigMap| Stores root CA certificates| -  
  
### Destination Controller

The `linkerd-destination` controller provides service discovery and traffic policy information to proxies. It aggregates data from multiple Kubernetes resource types and serves it via gRPC.

Component| Function| Port  
---|---|---  
`destination` container| Service discovery and policy serving| 8086 (gRPC)  
`EndpointsWatcher`| Watches Endpoints/EndpointSlices| -  
`WorkloadWatcher`| Watches Pod resources| -  
`ProfileWatcher`| Watches ServiceProfile resources| -  
  
Sources: [controller/api/destination/watcher/endpoints_watcher.go80-106](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/watcher/endpoints_watcher.go#L80-L106) [controller/api/destination/server.go44-61](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/server.go#L44-L61)

### Proxy Injector

The `linkerd-proxy-injector` is a Kubernetes admission webhook that automatically adds the `linkerd-proxy` sidecar and `linkerd-init` init container to pods in annotated namespaces.

Sources: [cli/cmd/testdata/install_default.golden457-494](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/testdata/install_default.golden#L457-L494)

## Data Plane Architecture

The data plane consists of lightweight proxies deployed as sidecar containers alongside application workloads. Each proxy handles all network traffic for its associated application pod.


Sources: [cli/cmd/testdata/install_default.golden1114-1153](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/testdata/install_default.golden#L1114-L1153) [controller/api/destination/endpoint_translator.go22-35](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/endpoint_translator.go#L22-L35)

### Proxy Components

Port| Purpose| Environment Variable  
---|---|---  
4143| Inbound proxy (receives redirected traffic)| `LINKERD2_PROXY_INBOUND_LISTEN_ADDR`  
4140| Outbound proxy (handles egress)| `LINKERD2_PROXY_OUTBOUND_LISTEN_ADDR`  
4191| Admin interface (metrics, health)| `LINKERD2_PROXY_ADMIN_LISTEN_ADDR`  
4190| Control plane gRPC| `LINKERD2_PROXY_CONTROL_LISTEN_ADDR`  
  
Sources: [controller/api/destination/endpoint_translator.go24-32](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/endpoint_translator.go#L24-L32)

## Service Discovery and Endpoint Management

The service discovery system watches Kubernetes resources and translates them into proxy-consumable endpoint information. The `EndpointsWatcher` is the core component that aggregates service and endpoint data.


Sources: [controller/api/destination/watcher/endpoints_watcher.go42-157](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/watcher/endpoints_watcher.go#L42-L157) [controller/api/destination/server.go44-61](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/server.go#L44-L61)

### Key Data Structures

The `EndpointsWatcher` uses several key data structures to manage service discovery state:

  * **`Address`** : Represents an individual endpoint with IP, port, associated Pod, and security identity
  * **`AddressSet`** : Collection of addresses for a service, including labels and traffic policy
  * **`ServiceID`** : Uniquely identifies a Kubernetes service by namespace and name
  * **`servicePublisher`** : Manages all ports for a single service
  * **`portPublisher`** : Manages listeners for a specific service:port combination



Sources: [controller/api/destination/watcher/endpoints_watcher.go42-157](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/watcher/endpoints_watcher.go#L42-L157)

## Component Interaction Flow

The following diagram shows how the major components interact during normal operation when a proxy requests service discovery information:


Sources: [controller/api/destination/watcher/endpoints_watcher.go247-265](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/watcher/endpoints_watcher.go#L247-L265) [controller/api/destination/server.go133-200](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/server.go#L133-L200)

### Configuration and State Management

The system configuration is primarily stored in the `linkerd-config` ConfigMap, which contains installation parameters and runtime settings for all components. Each controller reads this configuration on startup and uses it to configure watchers, networking, and security settings.

Sources: [cli/cmd/testdata/install_default.golden496-823](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/testdata/install_default.golden#L496-L823) [controller/cmd/destination/main.go50-150](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/cmd/destination/main.go#L50-L150)

This document describes Linkerd's control plane architecture, including its core components, their responsibilities, and how they interact to provide service mesh functionality. The control plane consists of several Kubernetes controllers and services that manage the data plane proxies and provide service discovery, identity management, and policy enforcement.

For information about the data plane proxies themselves, see [Data Plane](/linkerd/linkerd2/2.2-data-plane). For details about traffic policy management, see [Policy System](/linkerd/linkerd2/2.4-policy-system).

## Overview

The Linkerd control plane runs as a set of Kubernetes deployments in the `linkerd` namespace. It provides centralized management and coordination for the service mesh without being in the critical path of data plane traffic.

### Control Plane Architecture


Sources: [cli/cmd/testdata/install_default.golden1-2000](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/testdata/install_default.golden#L1-L2000) [controller/api/destination/server.go1-100](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/server.go#L1-L100)

## Identity Controller

The Identity Controller serves as the certificate authority for the mesh, providing mTLS identity to all meshed workloads.

### Identity Controller Components


The Identity Controller is deployed as the `linkerd-identity` deployment and runs the `identity` command from the controller binary. It has the following responsibilities:

  * **Certificate Issuance** : Issues short-lived certificates to workloads for mTLS authentication
  * **Trust Root Management** : Maintains the cluster's trust anchors in the `linkerd-identity-trust-roots` ConfigMap
  * **Token Validation** : Validates Kubernetes service account tokens through the TokenReview API



The controller requires permissions to create `tokenreviews` and manage `events`, as defined in the `linkerd-linkerd-identity` ClusterRole.

Sources: [cli/cmd/testdata/install_default.golden17-61](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/testdata/install_default.golden#L17-L61) [cli/cmd/testdata/install_default.golden839-1224](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/testdata/install_default.golden#L839-L1224)

## Destination Controller

The Destination Controller is the core service discovery component that provides endpoint information and traffic policies to the data plane proxies.

### Destination Controller Architecture


The Destination Controller runs as the `linkerd-destination` deployment and implements the `destination.DestinationServer` gRPC interface. Key components include:

### Core Server Structure

The main server is defined in the `server` struct in [controller/api/destination/server.go44-61](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/server.go#L44-L61):

  * **Configuration** : The `Config` struct contains cluster domain, trust domain, and feature flags
  * **Watchers** : Multiple specialized watchers monitor different Kubernetes resource types
  * **gRPC Endpoints** : Serves `Get()` for service discovery and `GetProfile()` for traffic profiles



### Endpoint Discovery

The `EndpointsWatcher` in [controller/api/destination/watcher/endpoints_watcher.go84-96](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/watcher/endpoints_watcher.go#L84-L96) is responsible for:

  * **Service Subscription** : Tracks subscriptions to specific services and ports via the `Subscribe()` method
  * **Address Resolution** : Converts Kubernetes endpoints to proxy-consumable address sets
  * **Update Propagation** : Notifies subscribers when endpoint sets change



### RBAC Permissions

The Destination Controller requires extensive permissions defined in the `linkerd-linkerd-destination` ClusterRole:

  * **Core Resources** : Read access to `pods`, `endpoints`, `services`, `nodes`
  * **Workload Resources** : Access to `replicasets`, `jobs`, `deployments`
  * **Linkerd Resources** : Access to `serviceprofiles`, `externalworkloads`
  * **EndpointSlice Management** : Full CRUD permissions for `endpointslices` when enabled



Sources: [controller/api/destination/server.go44-61](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/server.go#L44-L61) [controller/api/destination/watcher/endpoints_watcher.go84-96](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/watcher/endpoints_watcher.go#L84-L96) [cli/cmd/testdata/install_default.golden64-119](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/testdata/install_default.golden#L64-L119)

## Proxy Injector

The Proxy Injector automatically adds Linkerd proxy sidecars to pods via a Kubernetes mutating admission webhook.

### Proxy Injection Flow


The Proxy Injector operates through the following mechanism:

### Webhook Configuration

The `linkerd-proxy-injector-webhook-config` MutatingWebhookConfiguration intercepts `CREATE` operations on pods and services. It targets namespaces that:

  * Do not have `config.linkerd.io/admission-webhooks: disabled`
  * Are not system namespaces (`kube-system`, `cert-manager`)



### Injection Logic

When a pod creation is intercepted:

  1. **Annotation Check** : Verifies injection annotations on pods and namespaces
  2. **Proxy Container** : Adds the `linkerd-proxy` sidecar container
  3. **Init Container** : Adds the `linkerd-init` container for network setup (when not using CNI)
  4. **Volume Configuration** : Mounts necessary certificates and tokens



### RBAC Requirements

The injector requires permissions defined in `linkerd-linkerd-proxy-injector` ClusterRole:

  * **Resource Discovery** : Read access to various workload types (`deployments`, `pods`, etc.)
  * **Event Creation** : Ability to create events for audit logging

## Supporting Components

### Heartbeat

The Heartbeat component runs as a CronJob to periodically report cluster health and version information.

**Configuration** : Defined by the `linkerd-heartbeat` ServiceAccount and associated RBAC **Schedule** : Controlled by the `heartbeatSchedule` configuration value **Permissions** : Read access to `namespaces` and `serviceprofiles` for cluster analysis

### Validation Webhooks

Two ValidatingWebhookConfigurations ensure resource integrity:

  1. **Service Profile Validator** (`linkerd-sp-validator-webhook-config`): Validates ServiceProfile resources
  2. **Policy Validator** (`linkerd-policy-validator-webhook-config`): Validates policy.linkerd.io resources



Both are served by the Destination Controller and validate resources on `CREATE` and `UPDATE` operations.

### Identity Certificate Flow


The control plane components work together to provide:

  * **Continuous Discovery** : Endpoints and workloads are continuously monitored and updates streamed to proxies
  * **Secure Identity** : All proxies receive unique mTLS certificates for secure communication
  * **Policy Enforcement** : Traffic policies are validated and distributed to enforcement points
  * **Automatic Injection** : New workloads are automatically configured with proxy sidecars

The data plane in Linkerd2 consists of lightweight, high-performance proxies that are deployed as sidecar containers alongside application workloads. This document covers the proxy components, injection mechanisms, configuration system, and network initialization processes that enable transparent service mesh functionality.

For information about control plane components that manage the data plane, see [Control Plane](/linkerd/linkerd2/2.1-control-plane). For policy enforcement and traffic management, see [Policy System](/linkerd/linkerd2/2.4-policy-system).

## Overview

The Linkerd2 data plane operates through several key components that work together to provide service mesh capabilities:


**Data Plane Components Architecture**

This document explains Linkerd's service discovery system, which enables the data plane proxies to discover and connect to services in the Kubernetes cluster. Service discovery is implemented by the destination controller, which watches Kubernetes resources and provides real-time endpoint information to proxies via gRPC streams.

For information about traffic policy management and authorization, see [Policy System](/linkerd/linkerd2/2.4-policy-system). For details about the data plane proxy configuration, see [Data Plane](/linkerd/linkerd2/2.2-data-plane).

## Overview

Linkerd's service discovery system consists of several watchers that monitor different Kubernetes resources and a destination server that aggregates this information to provide endpoint data to proxies. The system supports both local services within the cluster and federated services across multiple clusters.


Sources: [controller/api/destination/server.go75-134](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/server.go#L75-L134) [controller/cmd/destination/main.go194-201](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/cmd/destination/main.go#L194-L201)

## Core Components

### DestinationServer

The `DestinationServer` is the central component that implements the destination gRPC API. It handles `Get` and `GetProfile` requests from proxies and manages subscriptions to various watchers.


Sources: [controller/api/destination/server.go136-289](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/server.go#L136-L289) [controller/api/destination/server.go675-711](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/server.go#L675-L711)

### EndpointsWatcher

The `EndpointsWatcher` monitors Kubernetes Services and their corresponding Endpoints or EndpointSlices. It maintains publishers for each service and port combination, notifying subscribers when endpoint sets change.

Key responsibilities:

  * Watch Service, Endpoints, and EndpointSlice resources
  * Maintain `servicePublisher` instances for each service
  * Handle endpoint filtering based on topology zones and traffic policies
  * Support both legacy Endpoints and newer EndpointSlice APIs




Sources: [controller/api/destination/watcher/endpoints_watcher.go84-106](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/watcher/endpoints_watcher.go#L84-L106) [controller/api/destination/watcher/endpoints_watcher.go116-149](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/watcher/endpoints_watcher.go#L116-L149)

### WorkloadWatcher

The `WorkloadWatcher` tracks individual pods and external workloads, providing detailed information about specific endpoints including their readiness, identity, and protocol configuration.


Sources: [controller/api/destination/watcher/workload_watcher.go28-62](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/watcher/workload_watcher.go#L28-L62) [controller/api/destination/watcher/workload_watcher.go112-130](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/watcher/workload_watcher.go#L112-L130)

## Service Discovery Flow

The service discovery process follows this sequence when a proxy requests endpoint information:


Sources: [controller/api/destination/server.go136-289](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/server.go#L136-L289) [controller/api/destination/endpoint_translator.go88-145](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/endpoint_translator.go#L88-L145)

## Address Translation and Filtering

The `endpointTranslator` component processes endpoint updates and applies various filters before sending them to proxies:

### Address Filtering Logic

  1. **IP Family Selection** \- Choose between IPv4 and IPv6 based on configuration
  2. **Zone-based Filtering** \- Route traffic to endpoints in the same topology zone when hints are available
  3. **Local Traffic Policy** \- Filter to node-local endpoints when `service.spec.internalTrafficPolicy` is set to `Local`
  4. **Endpoint Readiness** \- Only include ready endpoints in the address set




Sources: [controller/api/destination/endpoint_translator.go253-266](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/endpoint_translator.go#L253-L266) [controller/api/destination/endpoint_translator.go301-377](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/endpoint_translator.go#L301-L377)

## Profile Discovery

Service profiles provide routing and retry configuration for services. The `ProfileWatcher` monitors `ServiceProfile` resources and the destination server provides this information via the `GetProfile` RPC.


Sources: [controller/api/destination/server.go387-441](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/server.go#L387-L441) [controller/api/destination/server.go449-498](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/server.go#L449-L498)

## Integration Points

### Kubernetes Resource Watching

The destination controller uses Kubernetes informers to watch multiple resource types:

Resource Type| Watcher Component| Purpose  
---|---|---  
Service| `EndpointsWatcher`| Service definitions and port mappings  
Endpoints| `EndpointsWatcher`| Legacy endpoint information  
EndpointSlice| `EndpointsWatcher`| Modern endpoint information with topology hints  
Pod| `WorkloadWatcher`| Individual workload details and readiness  
ServiceProfile| `ProfileWatcher`| Traffic routing and retry configuration  
Server| `WorkloadWatcher`| Opaque protocol configuration  
ExternalWorkload| `WorkloadWatcher`| External mesh workloads  
  
Sources: [controller/api/destination/watcher/endpoints_watcher.go200-241](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/watcher/endpoints_watcher.go#L200-L241) [controller/api/destination/watcher/workload_watcher.go78-104](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/watcher/workload_watcher.go#L78-L104)

### Multicluster Federation

For federated services spanning multiple clusters, the `federatedServiceWatcher` handles both local and remote discovery:


Sources: [controller/api/destination/federated_service_watcher.go18-32](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/federated_service_watcher.go#L18-L32) [controller/api/destination/server.go193-240](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/controller/api/destination/server.go#L193-L240)

### External Workload Support

The system supports external workloads (non-Kubernetes workloads) through the `ExternalWorkload` CRD, enabling mesh expansion beyond the cluster boundaries.

  * [policy-test/Cargo.toml](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-test/Cargo.toml)



The Policy System is Linkerd's traffic policy management and authorization subsystem. It provides fine-grained control over service-to-service communication through policy enforcement, traffic routing, and access control mechanisms. The system consists of a Rust-based policy controller that watches Kubernetes resources and serves policy decisions to the Linkerd proxies via gRPC.

For service discovery mechanisms, see [Service Discovery](/linkerd/linkerd2/2.3-service-discovery). For overall control plane architecture, see [Control Plane](/linkerd/linkerd2/2.1-control-plane).

## Architecture Overview

The Policy System is implemented as a standalone controller (`linkerd-policy-controller`) that operates within the Linkerd control plane. It watches Kubernetes policy resources and translates them into actionable policies for the data plane proxies.

### Policy Controller Architecture


**Sources:** [policy-controller/src/main.rs1-19](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/src/main.rs#L1-L19) [policy-controller/runtime/Cargo.toml1-68](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/runtime/Cargo.toml#L1-L68) [policy-controller/core/Cargo.toml1-17](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/core/Cargo.toml#L1-L17) [policy-controller/grpc/Cargo.toml1-29](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/grpc/Cargo.toml#L1-L29)

## Core Components

### Policy Controller Runtime

The `linkerd-policy-controller-runtime` crate serves as the main orchestrator, handling command-line argument parsing, server initialization, and coordination between subsystems.

Component| Purpose| Key Dependencies  
---|---|---  
`Args::parse_and_run()`| CLI parsing and main execution| `clap`, `kubert`  
Runtime Server| HTTP/gRPC server management| `hyper`, `tonic`, `tower`  
Kubernetes Client| API server communication| `kube`, `k8s-openapi`  
  
### Policy Core

The `linkerd-policy-controller-core` crate contains the fundamental policy abstractions and business logic for authorization and routing decisions.


**Sources:** [policy-controller/core/Cargo.toml1-17](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/core/Cargo.toml#L1-L17)

### gRPC Policy Service

The `linkerd-policy-controller-grpc` crate implements the gRPC service interface used by Linkerd proxies to query policy decisions in real-time.

Service| Purpose| Protocol Buffer Definition  
---|---|---  
Inbound Policy| Authorization for incoming requests| `linkerd2-proxy-api` inbound  
Outbound Policy| Routing for outgoing requests| `linkerd2-proxy-api` outbound  
Policy Updates| Streaming policy changes| `async-stream`  
  
**Sources:** [policy-controller/grpc/Cargo.toml1-29](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/grpc/Cargo.toml#L1-L29)

## Kubernetes Integration

### Resource API Definitions

The `linkerd-policy-controller-k8s-api` crate defines Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs) and Kubernetes API structures for policy configuration.


**Sources:** [policy-controller/k8s/api/Cargo.toml1-28](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/k8s/api/Cargo.toml#L1-L28) [policy-controller/k8s/index/Cargo.toml1-40](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/k8s/index/Cargo.toml#L1-L40) [policy-controller/k8s/status/Cargo.toml1-35](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/k8s/status/Cargo.toml#L1-L35)

### Resource Indexing

The `linkerd-policy-controller-k8s-index` component maintains an in-memory index of Kubernetes resources relevant to policy decisions, using `kubert` for efficient resource watching.

Index Type| Resources Tracked| Update Mechanism  
---|---|---  
Service Index| `Service`, `Endpoints`| Kubernetes Watch API  
Policy Index| Policy CRDs| Custom Resource Watches  
Pod Index| `Pod` annotations and labels| Pod Watch Stream  
  
### Status Management

The `linkerd-policy-controller-k8s-status` component updates the status of policy resources to reflect their current state and any validation errors.

**Sources:** [policy-controller/k8s/index/Cargo.toml1-40](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/k8s/index/Cargo.toml#L1-L40) [policy-controller/k8s/status/Cargo.toml1-35](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/k8s/status/Cargo.toml#L1-L35)

## Policy Workflow

### Policy Decision Flow


**Sources:** [policy-controller/grpc/Cargo.toml9-22](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/grpc/Cargo.toml#L9-L22) [policy-controller/core/Cargo.toml8-16](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/core/Cargo.toml#L8-L16)

## Main Entry Point

The policy controller starts through a simple main function that initializes the crypto provider and delegates to the runtime:


The `linkerd_policy_controller_runtime::Args::parse_and_run()` method handles:

  * Command-line argument parsing via `clap`
  * Server initialization with `kubert`
  * gRPC service registration with `tonic`
  * Kubernetes client setup with `kube`



**Sources:** [policy-controller/src/main.rs1-19](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/src/main.rs#L1-L19) [policy-controller/runtime/Cargo.toml37-68](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/runtime/Cargo.toml#L37-L68)

## Dependencies and Integration

### Key External Dependencies

Dependency| Purpose| Usage  
---|---|---  
`kube`| Kubernetes client library| Resource watching and API operations  
`tonic`| gRPC framework| Policy service implementation  
`kubert`| Kubernetes utilities| Server framework and resource indexing  
`gateway-api`| Gateway API types| HTTPRoute and other Gateway resources  
`prometheus-client`| Metrics collection| Policy decision metrics  
  
### Memory Management

The policy controller uses `jemallocator` on x86_64 Linux for improved memory allocation performance, which is important given the large number of Kubernetes resources it tracks.

**Sources:** [policy-controller/Cargo.toml16-17](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/Cargo.toml#L16-L17) [policy-controller/src/main.rs4-6](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/src/main.rs#L4-L6) [Cargo.toml17-51](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/Cargo.toml#L17-L51)

## Testing Infrastructure

The `linkerd-policy-test` crate provides integration testing capabilities for policy scenarios, including:

  * Policy decision verification

  * Multi-cluster policy testing

This page provides an overview of the major components that make up the Linkerd2 service mesh. It describes the purpose, implementation, and relationships between core and extension components. For a higher-level architectural view, see [Architecture](/linkerd/linkerd2/2-architecture).

## Core Components Overview

Linkerd2 is composed of several distinct components that work together to provide service mesh functionality. These components can be categorized into control plane, data plane, user interfaces, and extensions.


**Diagram: Linkerd2 Component Overview**

Sources: [cli/cmd/root.go69-136](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/root.go#L69-L136) [Cargo.toml1-32](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/Cargo.toml#L1-L32)

## Component Technology Stack

Linkerd2 components are implemented across multiple languages with specific toolchain dependencies:


**Diagram: Technology Stack and Dependencies**

### Frontend Dependencies

Category| Key Dependencies| Purpose  
---|---|---  
UI Framework| `react@16.14.0`, `@material-ui/core@4.12.4`| Component library  
Visualization| `d3-force@3.0.0`, `d3-selection@3.0.0`| Network graphs  
Icons| `@fortawesome/react-fontawesome`| UI icons  
Internationalization| `@lingui/core@3.17.1`| Multi-language support  
Routing| `react-router-dom@5.3.4`| Navigation  
Build| `webpack@5.101.3`, `babel-loader`| Asset compilation  
Testing| `jest@30.1.3`, `enzyme@3.11.0`| Unit testing  
  
### CLI Implementation

The CLI uses the `cobra` command framework with:

  * Global flags for namespace and kubeconfig configuration
  * Extension system for modular commands (viz, multicluster, jaeger)
  * Kubernetes API integration
  * Version compatibility checking



Sources: [web/app/package.json6-42](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/package.json#L6-L42) [web/app/webpack.config.js12-89](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/webpack.config.js#L12-L89) [cli/cmd/root.go1-20](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/root.go#L1-L20) [web/app/.eslintrc1-94](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/.eslintrc#L1-L94) [bin/web1-131](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/bin/web#L1-L131)

## CLI Tool

The `linkerd` CLI is implemented in Go and provides the primary interface for Linkerd operations. The root command is defined in `NewRootCmd()` with comprehensive subcommand structure.


**Diagram: CLI Command Structure and Functions**

The CLI supports global flags including:

  * `--linkerd-namespace` (defaultLinkerdNamespace: "linkerd")
  * `--cni-namespace` (defaultCNINamespace: "linkerd-cni")
  * `--kubeconfig` for Kubernetes configuration
  * `--context` for kubeconfig context
  * `--api-addr` for direct control plane communication



Key CLI capabilities:

  * **Installation** : `install`, `install-cni-plugin`, `upgrade`
  * **Management** : `inject`, `uninject`, `profile`, `authz`
  * **Health** : `check`, `diagnostics`
  * **Identity** : Certificate and identity management
  * **Extensions** : Modular viz, multicluster, and jaeger commands



Sources: [cli/cmd/root.go72-144](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/root.go#L72-L144) [cli/cmd/version.go35-63](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/version.go#L35-L63)

## Control Plane

The control plane is the central nervous system of Linkerd2, orchestrating and managing the service mesh. It's implemented in Go and runs as a set of microservices in Kubernetes.


**Diagram: Control Plane Components**

The control plane consists of several key services:

  1. **Destination Service** : Provides service discovery information to the data plane proxies
  2. **Identity Service** : Manages mTLS certificates for secure communication
  3. **Proxy Injector** : Automatically injects sidecar proxies into application pods
  4. **Controller** : Manages overall mesh configuration
  5. **Admission Webhook** : Validates and mutates Kubernetes resources



The control plane runs in a dedicated namespace (by default `linkerd`) and serves as the coordination point for all service mesh functionality.

Sources: [cli/cmd/root.go21-29](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/root.go#L21-L29)

## Data Plane

The data plane consists of lightweight proxies written in Rust that are injected as sidecars into application pods. These proxies intercept and manage all network traffic to and from the application.


**Diagram: Data Plane Traffic Flow**

The data plane proxies are responsible for:

  * Transparently intercepting all TCP traffic to/from the application
  * Implementing service mesh features like load balancing, retries, and circuit breaking
  * Collecting metrics and telemetry data
  * Establishing and maintaining mTLS connections
  * Enforcing policies from the policy controller



The proxies are designed to be lightweight, with minimal resource utilization and latency impact.

Sources: [Cargo.toml1-32](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/Cargo.toml#L1-L32)

## Web Dashboard

The web dashboard is a React-based frontend built with Material-UI components. The main navigation is implemented in `NavigationBase` class with comprehensive sidebar structure.


**Diagram: Web Dashboard React Component Structure**

### Technology Stack

Component| Technology| Version  
---|---|---  
Frontend Framework| React| 16.14.0  
UI Library| Material-UI| 4.12.4  
Visualization| D3| 3.x (force, selection, drag)  
Build Tool| Webpack| 5.101.3  
Language Features| Babel| 7.28.4  
State Management| React Context| Built-in  
  
### Key React Components

  * **NavigationBase** : Main navigation with namespace selector and menu items
  * **NetworkGraphBase** : D3-based force-directed graph visualization using `forceSimulation`
  * **withREST** : Higher-order component for data fetching with polling
  * **ErrorSnackbar** : Material-UI based error display with `Snackbar` and `Slide` transitions



### Build Process

The web application uses Webpack configuration with:

  * Entry point: `./js/index.js`
  * Babel loader for JSX/ES6 transpilation
  * ESLint integration with Airbnb configuration
  * Hot reload via `webpack-dev-server`



Sources: [web/app/js/components/Navigation.jsx193-703](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/components/Navigation.jsx#L193-L703) [web/app/package.json6-117](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/package.json#L6-L117) [web/app/webpack.config.js12-89](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/webpack.config.js#L12-L89) [web/app/js/components/util/withREST.jsx16-144](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/components/util/withREST.jsx#L16-L144) [web/app/js/components/NetworkGraph.jsx45-229](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/components/NetworkGraph.jsx#L45-L229) [web/app/js/components/ErrorBanner.jsx36-104](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/components/ErrorBanner.jsx#L36-L104) [bin/web36-130](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/bin/web#L36-L130)

## Policy Controller

The policy controller enforces security and traffic policies within the service mesh. It's implemented in Rust and operates as a separate controller that integrates with the control plane.


**Diagram: Policy Controller Components**

The policy controller consists of several Rust crates:

  1. **Core** : Core types and traits for the policy controller
  2. **Runtime** : Main runtime for the controller
  3. **gRPC API** : API for communicating with data plane proxies
  4. **K8s API** : Kubernetes API client and resource definitions
  5. **K8s Index** : Indexing of Kubernetes resources
  6. **K8s Status** : Status reporting for policy resources



The policy controller:

  * Watches Kubernetes resources for policy definitions
  * Translates policies into configuration for data plane proxies
  * Provides API access for policy enforcement
  * Updates status on policy resources



Sources: [policy-controller/Cargo.toml1-22](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/Cargo.toml#L1-L22) [policy-controller/core/Cargo.toml1-17](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/core/Cargo.toml#L1-L17) [policy-controller/grpc/Cargo.toml1-27](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/grpc/Cargo.toml#L1-L27) [policy-controller/k8s/api/Cargo.toml1-24](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/k8s/api/Cargo.toml#L1-L24) [policy-controller/k8s/index/Cargo.toml1-35](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/k8s/index/Cargo.toml#L1-L35) [policy-controller/k8s/status/Cargo.toml1-30](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/k8s/status/Cargo.toml#L1-L30) [policy-controller/runtime/Cargo.toml1-74](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/runtime/Cargo.toml#L1-L74)

## Extension Components

Linkerd2 has a modular architecture that supports extensions for additional functionality.

### Viz Extension

The Viz extension provides metrics collection, visualization, and traffic monitoring capabilities:

  * Prometheus for metrics storage
  * Grafana for advanced dashboards (optional)
  * Web UI components for metrics visualization
  * Tap API for live traffic inspection



### MultiCluster Extension

The MultiCluster extension enables cross-cluster communication:

  * Gateway management for cross-cluster traffic
  * Service mirroring between clusters
  * Multi-cluster service discovery



### Jaeger Extension

The Jaeger extension provides distributed tracing:

  * Collection of trace data
  * Visualization of request flows across services
  * Integration with OpenTelemetry




**Diagram: Extension Components**

Sources: [cli/cmd/root.go123-136](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/root.go#L123-L136)

## Component Interactions

The components interact through well-defined APIs and interfaces implemented in the codebase:


**Diagram: Component API Interactions**

### Web Dashboard Data Flow

The dashboard implements a polling-based architecture using React patterns:


**Diagram: React Component Data Flow Patterns**

### CLI Command Execution

The CLI implements command patterns with:

  * `cobra.Command` structure for each subcommand
  * Global flags processed in `PersistentPreRunE`
  * Kubernetes API integration for cluster operations
  * Extension commands with `deprecateCmd()` wrapper for backward compatibility



### Error Handling Patterns

Components implement consistent error handling:

  * `handleApiError()` methods in React components
  * `ErrorSnackbar` for user-visible error display
  * API request cancellation via `cancelCurrentRequests()`
  * State management for `pendingRequests` and error states

## Error Handling and Health Checking

Linkerd2 includes robust error handling and health checking capabilities:


**Diagram: Error Handling and Health Checking**

The system provides:

  1. Comprehensive health checks via `linkerd check`
  2. Version compatibility verification between components
  3. Certificate validation for mTLS
  4. Error display and handling in the web UI
  5. Logging and diagnostic capabilities

The Linkerd CLI tool (`linkerd`) is the primary command-line interface for installing, configuring, and managing Linkerd service mesh deployments. It provides commands for installation, workload injection, upgrades, health checks, and observability features.

For information about the web dashboard interface, see [Web Dashboard](/linkerd/linkerd2/3.2-web-dashboard). For details about health checking functionality, see [Health Checker](/linkerd/linkerd2/3.4-health-checker).

## Architecture Overview

The CLI tool is built using the Cobra command framework and organized into a hierarchical command structure with core commands and extension commands.

### Command Structure


**Command Registration and Root Setup**

The main command structure is defined in `NewRootCmd()` which sets up global flags and adds all subcommands:

Sources: [cli/cmd/root.go72-145](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/root.go#L72-L145)

### Flag System Architecture


The flag system uses a layered approach where different command categories share common flags while maintaining command-specific options.

Sources: [cli/cmd/options.go30-33](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/options.go#L30-L33) [cli/cmd/root.go152-158](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/root.go#L152-L158)

## Core Commands

### Install Command

The `install` command generates Kubernetes manifests for deploying Linkerd control plane components.

**Command Flow:**


**Key Functions:**

  * `newCmdInstall()` \- Command definition and flag setup
  * `installControlPlane()` \- Main installation logic
  * `renderControlPlane()` \- Helm chart rendering
  * `renderCRDs()` \- Custom Resource Definition rendering



Sources: [cli/cmd/install.go90-188](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/install.go#L90-L188) [cli/cmd/install.go262-317](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/install.go#L262-L317)

### Inject Command

The `inject` command adds Linkerd proxy sidecars to Kubernetes workload resources.

**Injection Pipeline:**


**Key Components:**

  * `resourceTransformerInject` \- Handles resource transformation logic
  * `inject.ResourceConfig` \- Configuration for injection behavior
  * `inject.GetOverriddenValues` \- Value override logic for annotations



Sources: [cli/cmd/inject.go50-144](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/inject.go#L50-L144) [cli/cmd/inject.go154-237](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/inject.go#L154-L237)

### Upgrade Command

The `upgrade` command updates existing Linkerd installations while preserving configuration.

**Upgrade Process:**


The upgrade command loads previously stored configuration from the `linkerd-config-overrides` Secret and merges it with any new flags provided.

Sources: [cli/cmd/upgrade.go48-123](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/upgrade.go#L48-L123) [cli/cmd/upgrade.go264-298](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/upgrade.go#L264-L298)

## Resource Transformation System

The CLI tool uses a sophisticated resource transformation system for injection and uninjetion operations.

**ResourceConfig Architecture:**


**Key Classes and Functions:**

  * `inject.ResourceConfig` \- Central configuration object
  * `inject.NewResourceConfig()` \- Factory function
  * `inject.GetOverriddenValues()` \- Value resolution logic
  * `inject.ApplyAnnotationOverrides()` \- Annotation processing



Sources: [pkg/inject/inject.go552-567](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/pkg/inject/inject.go#L552-L567) [pkg/inject/inject.go193-206](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/pkg/inject/inject.go#L193-L206)

## Extension Integration

The CLI integrates with Linkerd extensions through a pluggable command system.

**Extension Command Structure:**


Extensions register their commands during CLI initialization and can provide their own flag sets and subcommands.

Sources: [cli/cmd/root.go124-128](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/root.go#L124-L128) [cli/cmd/root.go130-136](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/root.go#L130-L136)

## Configuration and Values System

The CLI uses a hierarchical configuration system based on Helm values with multiple override sources.

**Configuration Precedence:**


**Key Configuration Types:**

  * `l5dcharts.Values` \- Main configuration structure
  * `valuespkg.Options` \- Helm values override options
  * Annotation-based overrides for proxy configuration



Sources: [pkg/charts/linkerd2/values.go](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/pkg/charts/linkerd2/values.go) [cli/cmd/options.go33-127](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/options.go#L33-L127)

The Web Dashboard is a web-based user interface for monitoring and visualizing Linkerd service mesh deployments. It provides real-time metrics, resource topology visualization, and diagnostic tools to help operators understand and troubleshoot their service mesh.

This page documents the architecture and components of the Web Dashboard system. For information about using the dashboard, refer to the user documentation.

## System Architecture Overview

The Linkerd Web Dashboard consists of a Go backend server and a React-based frontend application. The backend serves the static frontend assets and provides API endpoints that the frontend uses to fetch metrics and resource information.

### Architecture Diagram


Sources: [web/main.go1-150](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/main.go#L1-L150) [web/srv/server.go1-150](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/srv/server.go#L1-L150) [web/app/js/index.js1-50](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/index.js#L1-L50)

### Component Interaction


Sources: [web/srv/api_handlers.go80-191](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/srv/api_handlers.go#L80-L191) [web/app/js/components/util/ApiHelpers.jsx59-150](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/components/util/ApiHelpers.jsx#L59-L150) [web/app/js/components/ResourceDetail.jsx50-120](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/components/ResourceDetail.jsx#L50-L120)

## Backend Server

The Web Dashboard backend is a Go HTTP server that provides:

  1. Static file serving for frontend assets
  2. API endpoints for metrics and resource data
  3. Proxying for Grafana and Jaeger integrations
  4. HTML template rendering



### Server Initialization

The backend server is initialized in `main.go` which:

  1. Parses command-line flags for configuration
  2. Sets up necessary API clients for metrics and Kubernetes
  3. Creates a health checker instance
  4. Initializes the server with all dependencies
  5. Starts serving HTTP requests



The server structure is defined in `web/srv/server.go`:


Sources: [web/main.go26-150](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/main.go#L26-L150) [web/srv/server.go33-63](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/srv/server.go#L33-L63) [web/srv/server.go82-146](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/srv/server.go#L82-L146)

### API Endpoints

The backend provides several API endpoints that the frontend uses to fetch data:

Endpoint| Description| Handler Function  
---|---|---  
`/api/version`| Returns version information| `handleAPIVersion`  
`/api/tps-reports`| Traffic performance summary metrics| `handleAPIStat`  
`/api/pods`| List of pods in the mesh| `handleAPIPods`  
`/api/services`| List of services in the mesh| `handleAPIServices`  
`/api/tap`| WebSocket endpoint for real-time tap data| `handleAPITap`  
`/api/routes`| Top routes information| `handleAPITopRoutes`  
`/api/edges`| Service dependency edges| `handleAPIEdges`  
`/api/check`| Health check results| `handleAPICheck`  
`/api/gateways`| Multi-cluster gateway information| `handleAPIGateways`  
  
The server also proxies requests to Grafana and Jaeger if these integrations are configured.

Sources: [web/srv/server.go146-221](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/srv/server.go#L146-L221) [web/srv/api_handlers.go36-62](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/srv/api_handlers.go#L36-L62) [web/srv/api_handlers.go96-101](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/srv/api_handlers.go#L96-L101) [web/srv/api_handlers.go133-191](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/srv/api_handlers.go#L133-L191)

## Frontend Application

The frontend is a single-page React application built with webpack. It provides:

  1. Navigation through different resources in the mesh
  2. Visualization of mesh topology and metrics
  3. Detailed views of individual resources
  4. Tables of performance metrics



### Application Initialization

The frontend application is initialized in `web/app/js/index.js`, which:

  1. Sets up the React application with context providers
  2. Configures React Router with routes matching the backend server routes
  3. Creates a central API helper for making requests to the backend
  4. Handles path prefix detection for Kubernetes proxying scenarios




Sources: [web/app/js/index.js78-115](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/index.js#L78-L115) [web/app/js/index.js117-226](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/index.js#L117-L226) [web/app/js/components/Navigation.jsx193-227](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/components/Navigation.jsx#L193-L227)

### Key Components

The dashboard is built from several key components:

  1. **Navigation** (`Navigation.jsx`): The main layout component that provides the sidebar, app bar, and context for the entire application.

  2. **ResourceDetail** (`ResourceDetail.jsx`): Displays detailed information about a specific resource (deployment, pod, service, etc.), including:

     * Success rate and request metrics
     * Pod health information
     * Upstream and downstream dependencies
     * Latency metrics
  3. **MetricsTable** (`MetricsTable.jsx`): Renders tables of performance metrics for resources, with columns including:

     * Success rate
     * Request rate
     * Latency percentiles (P50, P95, P99)
     * TCP metrics (connections, throughput)
  4. **Octopus** (`Octopus.jsx`): Visualizes the dependencies between resources, showing upstream and downstream connections with performance metrics.

  5. **ResourceList** (`ResourceList.jsx`): Shows a list of resources of a particular type with their basic metrics.

  6. **Namespace** (`Namespace.jsx`): Shows all resources within a namespace, grouped by resource type.




The frontend uses higher-order components like `withREST` to handle data fetching, caching, and polling logic.

Sources: [web/app/js/components/Navigation.jsx193-227](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/components/Navigation.jsx#L193-L227) [web/app/js/components/ResourceDetail.jsx51-146](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/components/ResourceDetail.jsx#L51-L146) [web/app/js/components/MetricsTable.jsx170-186](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/components/MetricsTable.jsx#L170-L186) [web/app/js/components/Octopus.jsx48-89](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/components/Octopus.jsx#L48-L89)

## Data Fetching and Metrics

The dashboard fetches metrics and resource data from the backend using a polling mechanism. Components regularly query for updated data and refresh the UI when new data arrives.

### API Helper

The `ApiHelpers` utility provides functions for making API requests to the backend:


This utility encapsulates the API communication logic, including:

  * Building URLs for different resources
  * Making cancelable requests
  * Handling errors
  * Managing polling intervals



Sources: [web/app/js/components/util/ApiHelpers.jsx59-200](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/components/util/ApiHelpers.jsx#L59-L200) [web/app/js/components/util/ApiHelpers.jsx260-287](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/components/util/ApiHelpers.jsx#L260-L287)

### Metrics Processing

The dashboard processes raw metrics data using utilities in `MetricUtils.jsx`. These functions transform the API response into a format suitable for display:

  1. **Success Rate** : Calculated from success and failure counts
  2. **Request Rate** : Calculated from total requests over the time window
  3. **Latency Percentiles** : Extracted from the latency distribution (P50, P95, P99)
  4. **TCP Metrics** : Processed for display in TCP-specific tables



The processed metrics are passed to components like `MetricsTable` for display.

Sources: [web/app/js/components/util/MetricUtils.jsx21-33](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/components/util/MetricUtils.jsx#L21-L33) [web/app/js/components/util/MetricUtils.jsx52-92](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/components/util/MetricUtils.jsx#L52-L92) [web/app/js/components/MetricsTable.jsx19-42](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/components/MetricsTable.jsx#L19-L42) [web/app/js/components/MetricsTable.jsx43-80](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/components/MetricsTable.jsx#L43-L80)

### Data Polling

Components use a polling mechanism to keep data up-to-date:


Most components implement their own polling or use the `withREST` higher-order component which provides generic polling functionality.

Sources: [web/app/js/components/ResourceDetail.jsx132-142](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/components/ResourceDetail.jsx#L132-L142) [web/app/js/components/util/withREST.jsx22-64](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/components/util/withREST.jsx#L22-L64)

## Routing and Navigation

The dashboard uses React Router for client-side routing. Routes are defined in `index.js` and mapped to their corresponding components.


The navigation sidebar provides links to these routes, allowing users to navigate between different views of the service mesh.

Sources: [web/app/js/index.js126-220](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/index.js#L126-L220) [web/srv/server.go146-190](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/srv/server.go#L146-L190)

## Integration with External Systems

The dashboard integrates with other systems to provide additional functionality:

### Grafana Integration

The dashboard can integrate with Grafana in two ways:

  1. **Internal Grafana** : Proxies requests to a Grafana instance running within the Linkerd deployment
  2. **External Grafana** : Links to an external Grafana instance



This integration allows users to access detailed metrics dashboards by clicking Grafana links from resource tables.

### Jaeger Integration

Similar to Grafana, the dashboard can proxy requests to a Jaeger instance for distributed tracing visualization. This integration is enabled when Jaeger is deployed as part of the Linkerd ecosystem.

Sources: [web/srv/server.go132-218](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/srv/server.go#L132-L218) [web/app/js/components/MetricsTable.jsx196-234](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/js/components/MetricsTable.jsx#L196-L234)

## Development and Building

The dashboard's frontend is built using webpack. The development workflow includes:

  1. Running a local development server with hot reloading
  2. Building production assets
  3. Running tests



The backend server is written in Go and can be run locally for development or deployed as part of the Linkerd control plane.

### Build Process

The build process for the frontend is configured in `webpack.config.js`:

  1. JSX files are transpiled using Babel
  2. Dependencies are bundled
  3. CSS is processed and included
  4. Assets are generated with hashed filenames for cache busting



The server loads the built frontend assets and serves them to users.

Sources: [web/app/webpack.config.js12-89](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/web/app/webpack.config.js#L12-L89) [bin/web1-131](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/bin/web#L1-L131)

## Summary

The Linkerd Web Dashboard is a React-based frontend application with a Go backend server that provides:

  1. Real-time metrics and resource information
  2. Resource topology visualization
  3. Detailed views of resources and their performance
  4. Integration with other observability tools



It communicates with the Linkerd Metrics API and Kubernetes API to gather data about the service mesh and presents this information in an intuitive user interface.

The Policy Controller is a Rust-based component that serves as the central policy management engine in the Linkerd control plane. It watches Kubernetes resources to build and maintain traffic policies, then serves these policies to data plane proxies via gRPC. The controller handles authorization policies, traffic routing rules, and service discovery information for the mesh.

For information about the overall control plane architecture, see [Control Plane](/linkerd/linkerd2/2.1-control-plane). For details about the Policy System concepts, see [Policy System](/linkerd/linkerd2/2.4-policy-system).

## Architecture Overview

The Policy Controller is implemented as a multi-module Rust workspace with distinct responsibilities for resource management, policy computation, and API serving.


**Sources:** [policy-controller/src/main.rs1-18](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/src/main.rs#L1-L18) [Cargo.toml1-52](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/Cargo.toml#L1-L52) [policy-controller/Cargo.toml1-18](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/Cargo.toml#L1-L18)

## Binary Structure and Initialization

The Policy Controller binary is a straightforward Rust application that sets up the runtime environment and delegates to the runtime module.


The main binary handles:

  * Memory allocator configuration using jemalloc on Linux x86_64
  * Cryptographic provider setup with aws-lc-rs for rustls
  * Argument parsing and runtime initialization



**Sources:** [policy-controller/src/main.rs4-17](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/src/main.rs#L4-L17) [policy-controller/Cargo.toml16-17](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/Cargo.toml#L16-L17)

## Core Modules

The Policy Controller is organized into specialized modules, each handling specific aspects of policy management:

Module| Purpose| Key Dependencies  
---|---|---  
`linkerd-policy-controller-runtime`| Command-line parsing, server coordination| `clap`, `kubert`, `tokio`  
`linkerd-policy-controller-k8s-index`| Kubernetes resource watching and indexing| `kube`, `kubert`, `tokio`  
`linkerd-policy-controller-core`| Policy computation and business logic| `ahash`, `http`, `ipnet`  
`linkerd-policy-controller-grpc`| gRPC API implementation for proxies| `tonic`, `linkerd2-proxy-api`  
`linkerd-policy-controller-k8s-api`| Custom Resource Definitions| `k8s-openapi`, `schemars`  
`linkerd-policy-controller-k8s-status`| Status condition management| `kubert`, `parking_lot`  
  
**Sources:** [policy-controller/runtime/Cargo.toml1-68](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/runtime/Cargo.toml#L1-L68) [policy-controller/k8s/index/Cargo.toml1-40](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/k8s/index/Cargo.toml#L1-L40) [policy-controller/core/Cargo.toml1-17](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/core/Cargo.toml#L1-L17) [policy-controller/grpc/Cargo.toml1-29](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/grpc/Cargo.toml#L1-L29) [policy-controller/k8s/api/Cargo.toml1-28](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/k8s/api/Cargo.toml#L1-L28) [policy-controller/k8s/status/Cargo.toml1-35](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/k8s/status/Cargo.toml#L1-L35)

## Kubernetes Integration

The Policy Controller deeply integrates with Kubernetes through resource watching, custom resources, and status management.


The `k8s-index` module uses the `kube` crate's `Controller` pattern to watch multiple resource types and maintain an eventually-consistent view of the cluster state. Changes trigger events that flow to the policy computation engine.

**Sources:** [policy-controller/k8s/index/Cargo.toml24-31](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/k8s/index/Cargo.toml#L24-L31) [policy-controller/k8s/api/Cargo.toml9-27](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/k8s/api/Cargo.toml#L9-L27) [policy-controller/k8s/status/Cargo.toml24-30](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/k8s/status/Cargo.toml#L24-L30)

## Policy Computation Engine

The core module implements the business logic for converting Kubernetes resources into executable traffic policies.


The core engine operates asynchronously using `futures` and `async-trait`, building policies incrementally as resources change. It uses `ahash` for efficient indexing and `ipnet` for network address operations.

**Sources:** [policy-controller/core/Cargo.toml8-16](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/core/Cargo.toml#L8-L16)

## gRPC API Service

The Policy Controller exposes a gRPC API that implements the `linkerd2-proxy-api` contract for serving policies to data plane proxies.


The gRPC module serves streaming APIs where proxies can watch for policy changes. It uses `async-stream` to handle long-lived connections and `drain` for graceful shutdown coordination.

**Sources:** [policy-controller/grpc/Cargo.toml9-28](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/grpc/Cargo.toml#L9-L28)

## Resource Management and Status

The Policy Controller maintains bidirectional communication with Kubernetes, both consuming resources and updating their status conditions.


The status module uses `kubert`'s lease mechanism for leader election, ensuring only one Policy Controller instance updates resource status at a time. It employs `parking_lot` for efficient synchronization and `prometheus-client` for observability.

**Sources:** [policy-controller/k8s/status/Cargo.toml24-30](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/k8s/status/Cargo.toml#L24-L30) [policy-controller/runtime/Cargo.toml47-58](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/runtime/Cargo.toml#L47-L58)

## Testing Infrastructure

The Policy Controller includes comprehensive testing through the `policy-test` workspace member.

Test Type| Implementation| Key Dependencies  
---|---|---  
Unit Tests| Module-level testing| `tokio-test`, `maplit`  
Integration Tests| Full controller testing| `k3d`, `kube` client  
Policy Tests| End-to-end scenarios| `linkerd2-proxy-api`, `tonic`  
Gateway API Tests| External standard compliance| `gateway-api` with experimental features  
  
The test suite validates policy computation, Kubernetes integration, and gRPC API correctness using realistic cluster scenarios.

**Sources:** [policy-test/Cargo.toml1-48](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-test/Cargo.toml#L1-L48) [policy-controller/k8s/index/Cargo.toml33-40](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/policy-controller/k8s/index/Cargo.toml#L33-L40)

# Health Checker

Relevant source files

  * [cli/cmd/check.go](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/check.go)

The Health Checker is Linkerd's comprehensive validation system that diagnoses installation and operational issues across the control plane, data plane, and cluster configuration. It powers the `linkerd check` command and provides structured health validation through categorized checks with retry mechanisms and detailed error reporting.

For information about the CLI tool that uses this system, see [CLI Tool](/linkerd/linkerd2/3.1-cli-tool). For details about installation validation, see [Installation](/linkerd/linkerd2/4.1-installation).

## Architecture Overview

The Health Checker follows a hierarchical architecture where checks are organized into categories, each containing multiple individual validation functions. The system uses an observer pattern to report results and supports various execution modes.


Sources: [pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go414-455](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go#L414-L455) [pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go515-1500](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go#L515-L1500) [cli/cmd/check.go92-227](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/check.go#L92-L227)

## Core Components

### HealthChecker Structure

The `HealthChecker` struct serves as the main orchestrator, containing categories of checks and execution options:

Field| Type| Purpose  
---|---|---  
`categories`| `[]*Category`| Ordered list of check categories  
`Options`| `*Options`| Configuration including namespaces and timeouts  
`kubeAPI`| `*k8s.KubernetesAPI`| Kubernetes client for cluster operations  
`controlPlanePods`| `[]corev1.Pod`| Cached control plane pod information  
`LatestVersions`| `version.Channels`| Version information for updates  
  
Sources: [pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go414-429](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go#L414-L429)

### Category and Checker Model

Individual checks are organized into categories using this hierarchy:


Sources: [pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go368-391](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go#L368-L391) [pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go275-350](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go#L275-L350)

## Check Categories

The health checker includes multiple predefined categories that validate different aspects of the Linkerd installation:

### Core Infrastructure Checks

Category ID| Purpose| Key Validations  
---|---|---  
`KubernetesAPIChecks`| Kubernetes connectivity| API client initialization, cluster access  
`KubernetesVersionChecks`| Version compatibility| Minimum Kubernetes version requirements  
`LinkerdPreInstallChecks`| Pre-installation validation| Permissions, namespace availability, clock skew  
  
### Control Plane Checks

Category ID| Purpose| Key Validations  
---|---|---  
`LinkerdConfigChecks`| Configuration validation| RBAC, CRDs, webhooks, service accounts  
`LinkerdControlPlaneExistenceChecks`| Control plane health| Pod status, replica sets, cluster networks  
`LinkerdIdentity`| Certificate validation| Trust anchors, issuer certificates, expiration  
`LinkerdWebhooksAndAPISvcTLS`| Webhook certificates| Proxy injector, service profile validator  
  
### Data Plane and Versioning

Category ID| Purpose| Key Validations  
---|---|---  
`LinkerdDataPlaneChecks`| Data plane health| Proxy readiness, version consistency, labels  
`LinkerdVersionChecks`| Version management| Latest version detection, CLI updates  
`LinkerdControlPlaneVersionChecks`| Version consistency| Control plane vs CLI version matching  
  
Sources: [pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go48-143](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go#L48-L143) [pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go515-1500](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go#L515-L1500)

## Check Execution Flow

The health checker implements a sophisticated execution model with retry logic and error categorization:


Sources: [pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go1552-1628](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go#L1552-L1628)

### Retry Mechanism

Checks support configurable retry behavior through deadline-based retries:


Sources: [pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go1582-1628](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go#L1582-L1628) [pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go194-198](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go#L194-L198)

## Error Types and Handling

The health checker defines several specialized error types for different check outcomes:

Error Type| Purpose| Example Usage  
---|---|---  
`SkipError`| Check should be ignored| CNI checks when CNI disabled  
`CategoryError`| Error with category context| Distinguishing between error sources  
`ResourceError`| Resource-specific errors| Missing Kubernetes resources  
`VerboseSuccess`| Success with additional info| Detailed status messages  
  
Sources: [pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go234-273](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/pkg/healthcheck/healthcheck.go#L234-L273)

## Integration with CLI

The `linkerd check` command provides multiple execution modes that configure different sets of health checks:


Sources: [cli/cmd/check.go129-227](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/check.go#L129-L227) [cli/cmd/check.go139-187](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/check.go#L139-L187)

### CLI Options Configuration

The `checkOptions` struct configures health checker behavior:

Option| Flag| Purpose  
---|---|---  
`preInstallOnly`| `--pre`| Run only pre-installation checks  
`crdsOnly`| `--crds`| Check only CRD installation  
`dataPlaneOnly`| `--proxy`| Focus on data plane validation  
`namespace`| `--namespace`| Limit data plane checks to specific namespace  
`wait`| `--wait`| Maximum time for checks to pass  
`output`| `--output`| Output format (table, json, short)  
  
Sources: [cli/cmd/check.go25-49](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/check.go#L25-L49) [cli/cmd/check.go52-74](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/check.go#L52-L74)

## Extension Integration

The health checker supports dynamic extension discovery and validation:


The system automatically discovers Linkerd extensions by:

  1. Scanning cluster namespaces for `linkerd.io/extension` labels
  2. Finding corresponding `linkerd-{extension}` binaries in the system PATH
  3. Executing extension-specific health checks with inherited CLI flags

This document covers the deployment patterns, installation processes, and configuration management for Linkerd. It focuses on how Linkerd is deployed to Kubernetes clusters through the CLI and Helm charts, including the control plane installation, CRD management, and upgrade procedures.

For specific installation commands and procedures, see [Installation](/linkerd/linkerd2/4.1-installation). For detailed Helm chart configuration, see [Helm Charts](/linkerd/linkerd2/4.2-helm-charts). For proxy sidecar injection mechanisms, see [Proxy Injection](/linkerd/linkerd2/4.3-proxy-injection).

## Deployment Architecture Overview

Linkerd deployment follows a two-phase installation model: CRDs first, then the control plane. The deployment system is built around Helm charts that are rendered through the CLI rather than requiring Helm directly.


Sources: [cli/cmd/install.go90-188](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/install.go#L90-L188) [cli/cmd/upgrade.go48-123](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/upgrade.go#L48-L123) [cli/cmd/install.go330-376](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2/blob/adfdb340/cli/cmd/install.go#L330-L376)

The installation process is orchestrated by the `linkerd install` command, which validates the cluster state, processes configuration, and renders Kubernetes manifests.

---|---|---|---

CLI Flags| Medium| `makeInstallUpgradeFlags()`| `--ha`, `--proxy-version`  
Helm Values| High| `--set`, `--values`| Custom overrides  
Value Files| Highest| `--set-file`| External config files
