This page documents the testing and fuzzing infrastructure used in the linkerd2-proxy codebase. It covers the integration testing framework, unit testing approaches, and fuzzing infrastructure. For information about the CI/CD pipeline that runs these tests, see [CI/CD Pipeline](/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/7.3-cicd-pipeline).

## Overview

The linkerd2-proxy codebase employs a comprehensive testing strategy that includes:

  1. **Integration tests** : End-to-end tests that validate the behavior of the proxy in various scenarios
  2. **Unit tests** : Component-level tests that verify individual modules work correctly
  3. **Fuzzing** : Automated generation of test inputs to discover edge cases and potential vulnerabilities



## Integration Testing Framework

The integration testing framework provides a robust environment for testing the proxy's behavior under various conditions. It includes mocks for services, controllers, and clients, as well as utilities for setting up test environments.

### Architecture


Sources:

  * [linkerd/app/integration/src/lib.rs1-301](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/linkerd/app/integration/src/lib.rs#L1-L301)

### Key Components

#### Test Environment (`TestEnv`)

The test environment provides a way to configure the proxy with specific environment variables. This is crucial for testing different configurations and behaviors.

#### Server Mocks

The server mocks simulate backend services that the proxy connects to. They can be configured to:

  1. Respond to specific HTTP paths with predefined responses
  2. Add latency to responses
  3. Run different protocol servers (HTTP/1, HTTP/2, TCP)
  4. Simulate failures and connection issues




Sources:

  * [linkerd/app/integration/src/server.rs1-366](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/linkerd/app/integration/src/server.rs#L1-L366)



#### Client Mocks

The client mocks simulate clients that send requests through the proxy. They support:

  1. HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 protocols
  2. TLS configuration
  3. Request building and response handling
  4. Connection management




Sources:

  * [linkerd/app/integration/src/client.rs1-368](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/linkerd/app/integration/src/client.rs#L1-L368)



#### Controller Mocks

The controller mocks simulate the control plane services that the proxy communicates with, such as:

  1. Destination service for service discovery
  2. Identity service for TLS certificates
  3. Policy service for authorization policies




Sources:

  * [linkerd/app/integration/src/controller.rs1-409](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/linkerd/app/integration/src/controller.rs#L1-L409)



#### Proxy Builder and Runner

The proxy builder provides a fluent API for configuring and starting a proxy instance for testing:

The metrics validation utilities help assert that the proxy is correctly emitting metrics:

  1. Set up a test environment

## Testing Utilities

### Assertion Macros

The codebase includes several custom assertion macros to simplify testing:

  1. `assert_eventually!` \- Retry an assertion until it succeeds or times out
  2. `assert_contains!` \- Assert that a string contains a substring
  3. `assert_eventually_contains!` \- Combine the above two macros



These macros help handle asynchronous behavior and timing issues in tests.

Sources:

  * [linkerd/app/integration/src/lib.rs50-154](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/linkerd/app/integration/src/lib.rs#L50-L154)



### Timeout and Retry Mechanisms

The testing framework includes utilities for dealing with timing and retries:

  1. `DEFAULT_TEST_PATIENCE` \- Default duration to wait between retries
  2. `ENV_TEST_PATIENCE_MS` \- Environment variable to override the patience duration

  * [linkerd/app/integration/src/lib.rs50-70](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/linkerd/app/integration/src/lib.rs#L50-L70)



## Fuzzing Infrastructure

Fuzzing is used to discover edge cases and potential vulnerabilities by automatically generating test inputs. The project uses `libfuzzer-sys` for fuzzing various components.

### Fuzzing Architecture


Sources:

### Fuzzing Targets

The project includes several fuzzing targets for different components:

---|---|---

DNS| `linkerd/dns/fuzz`| Tests DNS resolution and parsing  
Transport Header| `linkerd/transport-header/fuzz`| Tests transport header parsing and processing

  * [linkerd/transport-header/fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_target_structured.rs1-17](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/linkerd/transport-header/fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_target_structured.rs#L1-L17)

### Fuzzing Workflow

The typical fuzzing workflow includes:

  1. Setting up a fuzzing target
  2. Configuring tracing (usually disabled for performance)
  3. Creating a Tokio runtime
  4. Processing the fuzz input data
  5. Running the component's fuzzing logic
  6. Checking for crashes or unexpected behavior




Sources:

  * [linkerd/app/inbound/fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_target_1.rs1-23](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/linkerd/app/inbound/fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_target_1.rs#L1-L23)
  * [linkerd/dns/fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_target_1.rs1-21](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/linkerd/dns/fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_target_1.rs#L1-L21)



## Running Tests

### Integration Tests

Integration tests can be run using the standard Rust test runner:
    
    
    cargo test --package linkerd-app-integration
    

You can run specific tests by providing the test name:
    
    
    cargo test --package linkerd-app-integration inbound_http1
    

### Fuzzing

To run the fuzzing tests, you need to use the `cargo-fuzz` tool:
    
    
    cargo install cargo-fuzz
    cargo fuzz run fuzz_target_1 --package linkerd-app-inbound-fuzz
    

Some fuzzing tests have specific configuration options:
    
    
    RUST_LOG=trace cargo fuzz run fuzz_target_structured --package linkerd-transport-header-fuzz
    

## Metrics Testing

The proxy emits metrics that can be validated in tests. The test framework includes utilities for checking metrics and their values.

### Metric Assertion Pattern

    metric("request_total")

## Common Testing Patterns

### Setup and Teardown

Most tests follow a pattern of:

  1. Setting up a server with specific routes
  2. Creating a controller with mock behavior
  3. Starting a proxy with the desired configuration
  4. Running assertions against the proxy
  5. Cleaning up resources



### Testing Error Handling

The test framework includes patterns for testing error handling:

  1. Testing timeouts and retries
  2. Testing connection failures
  3. Testing protocol errors
  4. Testing TLS negotiation failures

### Testing HTTP Behavior

  1. Testing HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 protocols

This document describes the Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline for the linkerd2-proxy. It covers how code changes are tested, built, and released through automated processes powered by GitHub Actions. For information about the local build system, see [Build System](/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/7.1-build-system).

## Overview

The linkerd2-proxy project uses GitHub Actions as its primary CI/CD platform. The pipeline ensures code quality through automated testing and validation, and facilitates the release of new proxy versions that can be integrated into the broader Linkerd ecosystem.


Sources: [.github/workflows/release.yml1-238](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/.github/workflows/release.yml#L1-L238) [.github/workflows/pr.yml1-178](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/.github/workflows/pr.yml#L1-L178) [.github/workflows/release-weekly.yml1-79](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/.github/workflows/release-weekly.yml#L1-L79)

## Continuous Integration

The continuous integration process is primarily driven by pull requests to the repository. Different workflows are triggered based on the type of changes made.

### Pull Request Workflow

When a pull request is opened or updated, the following workflow is executed:


Sources: [.github/workflows/pr.yml14-178](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/.github/workflows/pr.yml#L14-L178)

The pull request workflow performs several checks:

  1. **Meta Analysis** : Determines what types of files have changed to decide which checks to run

  2. **GitHub Actions Validation** : Lints workflow files and ensures action references are up-to-date

  3. **Rust Code Checks** : Performs various validations on Rust code:

     * Formatting checks (via rustfmt)
     * Clippy linting
     * Documentation generation
     * Dependency audit (cargo deny)
     * Compilation and tests
  4. **Crate-specific Checks** : Runs targeted checks on specific crates that have been modified

  5. **Linkerd Install Test** : Builds the proxy Docker image and tests installing it as part of Linkerd




If all checks pass, the PR is ready for review and merging. For PRs from Dependabot, the workflow will automatically merge them if all checks pass.

Sources: [.github/workflows/pr.yml74-178](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/.github/workflows/pr.yml#L74-L178)

### Code Quality Checks

Several specialized workflows ensure code quality:

#### Coverage Analysis

The coverage workflow measures test coverage and reports results to Codecov:


Sources: [.github/workflows/coverage.yml1-59](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/.github/workflows/coverage.yml#L1-L59)

#### Fuzz Testing

The fuzzing workflow runs for PRs that touch specific security-critical crates:


Sources: [.github/workflows/fuzzers.yml1-64](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/.github/workflows/fuzzers.yml#L1-L64)

#### Rust Toolchain Testing

The project also maintains workflows to test against beta and nightly Rust toolchains to catch potential issues with upcoming Rust versions:

  1. **Beta Testing** : Weekly tests against the beta Rust channel
  2. **Nightly Testing** : Daily tests against the nightly Rust channel



Sources: [.github/workflows/nightly.yml1-35](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/.github/workflows/nightly.yml#L1-L35) [.github/workflows/beta.yml1-35](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/.github/workflows/beta.yml#L1-L35)

## Continuous Deployment

The continuous deployment process handles building, packaging, and releasing new versions of the proxy.

### Release Process

The release workflow can be triggered manually via workflow dispatch or by a pull request:


Sources: [.github/workflows/release.yml1-238](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/.github/workflows/release.yml#L1-L238) [.github/workflows/release-weekly.yml1-79](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/.github/workflows/release-weekly.yml#L1-L79)

The release process includes:

  1. **Meta Configuration** : Sets up version, architectures, and platforms to build for
  2. **Package Building** : Creates packages for multiple architectures (amd64, arm64, arm) and platforms (Linux, Windows)
  3. **Publishing** : Creates a GitHub release with the built artifacts
  4. **Linkerd Integration** : Triggers the `sync-proxy.yml` workflow in the linkerd/linkerd2 repository to update the proxy version



Sources: [.github/workflows/release.yml125-170](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/.github/workflows/release.yml#L125-L170) [.github/workflows/release.yml171-223](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/.github/workflows/release.yml#L171-L223)

### Automated Weekly Releases

The project includes an automated weekly release mechanism:

  1. Runs on a weekly schedule (Wednesday nights)
  2. Checks if a release has been made in the last 72 hours
  3. If no recent release exists and new commits have been made since the last release, triggers a new minor version release



Sources: [.github/workflows/release-weekly.yml1-79](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/.github/workflows/release-weekly.yml#L1-L79)

## Build Configuration

The build process utilizes various configuration parameters to customize builds:

### Build Parameters

Parameter| Description| Default  
---|---|---  
`profile`| Build profile (debug/release)| `"release"` for releases  
`version`| Version in semver format| Required for releases  
`tag-prefix`| Prefix for Git tag| `"release/"`  
`publish`| Whether to publish the release| `false`  
`prerelease`| Whether this is a prerelease| `false`  
`draft`| Whether this is a draft release| `false`  
`latest`| Whether to mark as latest release| `true`  
  
These parameters can be specified when manually triggering a release workflow.

Sources: [.github/workflows/release.yml6-46](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/.github/workflows/release.yml#L6-L46)

### Cross-Platform Building

The project supports building for multiple platforms:


Sources: [.github/workflows/release.yml125-170](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/.github/workflows/release.yml#L125-L170) [justfile30-48](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/justfile#L30-L48)

The build matrix includes:

  * **Architectures** : amd64, arm64, arm
  * **Operating Systems** : Linux, Windows
  * **libc types** : GNU (with plans for musl)



Note that certain combinations are excluded, such as Windows on arm platforms.

Sources: [.github/workflows/release.yml129-138](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/.github/workflows/release.yml#L129-L138)

## Integration with Linkerd

When a new proxy version is released, it can be automatically integrated with the main Linkerd project:

  1. After a successful release (that is not marked as a prerelease or draft), the workflow triggers the `sync-proxy.yml` workflow in the linkerd/linkerd2 repository
  2. This causes the main Linkerd project to update its reference to the proxy version



Sources: [.github/workflows/release.yml213-222](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/.github/workflows/release.yml#L213-L222)

## Development Workflows

The CI/CD pipeline also supports various development workflows:

### Shell and Markdown Linting

Dedicated workflows check shell scripts and markdown files for correctness:

  * **Shell Linting** : Uses shellcheck to validate shell scripts
  * **Markdown Linting** : Ensures markdown files follow best practices



Sources: [.github/workflows/shellcheck.yml1-21](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/.github/workflows/shellcheck.yml#L1-L21) [.github/workflows/markdown.yml1-21](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/.github/workflows/markdown.yml#L1-L21)

### Toolchain Validation

A specialized workflow validates that the Rust toolchain version is consistent across:

  1. The `rust-toolchain.toml` file
  2. The development container configuration
  3. GitHub Actions workflows that specify Rust versions



Sources: [.github/workflows/toolchain.yml1-67](https://github.com/linkerd/linkerd2-proxy/blob/ff162dba/.github/workflows/toolchain.yml#L1-L67)
